subject: Renewal: Ultima Inc — Contract renewal and concession request
messages:
From: Alex Cullen <acullen@ultimainc.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal discussion — usage dip and request for concessions

Hi Sergio,

Hope you had a great weekend. Ultima's renewal is up at the end of this year and our Execs have asked me to consolidate spend across fewer vendors. Our Q3 usage with Redwood was lower than forecast (attached) and the CFO is pushing to get better economics if we're going to continue the relationship.

Specifically, they're asking if Redwood can:
- Offer a 20% first-year renewal discount (applied to base subscription),
- Provide a one-time credit equal to two months' invoice, and
- Reset the billing term to start Jan 1 to align with our fiscal year.

There's also a competing PoC scheduled for December — if we can't get closer on price/terms we may move forward with that.

Can you let me know what flexibility you have? Happy to hop on a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Alex Cullen
Head of Cloud Platform
Ultima Inc

(attachment: Ultima_usage_q3.pdf (pdf))

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Alex Cullen <acullen@ultimainc.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — usage dip and request for concessions

Alex —

Really appreciate the heads-up and the usage file. I get the timing pressure given the competing PoC. We're committed to long-term partnerships and want to find a path that keeps Ultima on Redwood without compromising our pricing guardrails.

Quick proposal: can we do a short internal review and come back with a formal concession package by Wednesday? If you're available, I can book a 30-min call tomorrow to align on priorities (price vs. term vs. credits).

Looping in Laura and Marissa to review financial and CS impacts.

Cheers,
Sergio
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal discussion — request for concessions (details & ask)

Team — forwarding Alex's note and usage. Bottom line: Ultima is looking for material concessions to avoid switching. My read: high strategic value (they're in finance/infra), but current ACV is $420k ARR; conceding too much sets a bad precedent.

I believe a defensible package to keep them would be:
- 20% discount year 1 (conditional),
- One-time credit equal to 2 months' average invoice OR 2 months of prepaid service credit,
- Billing term reset to Jan 1 (aligns with their FY, minimal operational effort),
- Add a 3-month SLA credit (if we miss agreed latency/uptime SLOs) as a goodwill item.

Estimated P&L impact: ~14% ARR erosion in year 1 if we accept the above. Alternate ask: 15% discount + 2-month credit reduces impact to ~10% and might be easier to approve.

Attachments: proposed-offer-ultima-20261103.pdf (draft SOW + pricing grid).

Requesting: Laura / Vivek — can you authorize one of the two packages below (I and II) or advise modifications so I can go back to Alex? Need sign-off by COB Thu to stay ahead of their internal procurement window.

I. Preferred: 20% discount + 2-month credit + Jan 1 term reset + 3-month SLA credit (internal approval required: Exec sign-off)
II. Compromise: 15% discount + 2-month credit + Jan 1 term reset + 3-month SLA credit (Finance + RevOps approval)

Thanks —
Sergio

(attachment: proposed-offer-ultima-20261103.pdf)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal discussion — request for concessions (details & ask)

Sergio / Laura —

Thanks for the breakdown. A few thoughts:
- We should avoid a straight 20% list discount if possible. Prefer a structured package that preserves list pricing (e.g., term commit + discount + one-time credit) so we don't create a precedent for simple percent cuts.
- The Jan 1 term reset is reasonable operationally but impacts revenue recognition and may require an accounting memo. Loop Finance/RevOps (I've cc'd Neha).
- SLA credit: fine as a short-term goodwill item (3 months) but needs legal to sign off on the exact SLO triggers.

Proposal from me: approve II (15% + 2-month credit + Jan 1 reset + 3-month SLA credit) pending RevOps sign-off. If the customer pushes hard on 20% we escalate to Exec (Laura) for final sign-off.

Vivek
VP, Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference

All —

I've reviewed the proposed packages and P&L impact. Given Ultima's strategic footprint (Finance platform) and the short timeline, I'm authorizing the compromise package with a tightened guardrail:

Approved concession (conditional):
- 15% first-year discount on base subscription (applies to the first 12 months only)
- One-time credit equal to two months' average invoice (applied to the first invoice after renewal)
- Billing term reset to Jan 1, 2027 (one-time alignment, requires RevOps runbook)
- 3-month SLA credit as a goodwill remedy (legal to define triggers)

Conditions:
1) Customer must sign the updated SOW and 12-month renewal by Nov 19, 2026.
2) Discounts/credits are one-time and non-precedential (document clause required).
3) RevOps/Finance (Neha) to confirm revenue recognition impact and post the accounting memo before final contract execution.
4) Legal to review SLA language; Marissa to coordinate.

Marissa/Neha: please confirm you can operationalize by EOD Monday (11/8). Sergio — share the updated draft with Alex once we have the accounting checklist and legal language.

Laura Bennett
GM, North America Sales | Redwood Inference
